CTS-A-O · REPRODUCIBLE OFFLINE AUDIT · 29 OCTOBER 2026

Main PF: validation, execution and close reasons

Eight fixed symbols. 7–8 October: 24h evaluated prehistory. 8–9 October: 24h trading. An additional 24h initializes indicators only. All used market data fits within 72 hours. This is a bounded diagnostic parameter grid, not a full factory-grid pass or exchange execution.

Trading performance remains poor. The report fixes do not improve returns. The repeated run retains every funded close, open holding, allocation and loss. A passing historical PF cannot guarantee the PF of later trades. The persistent Base → own Main → own Real → Active adapter is still pending integration in draft #219.

Measured cohorts

Confirmed reporting repairs

  1. Validation uses an equal-weight mean of independently passing sets. No-loss sets are counted separately; the engine's finite no-loss gate score is never averaged as a measured PF.
  2. Closed execution PF uses closed orders only. Open holdings retain their own mark-inclusive statistics and counts.
  3. Lane, range, type and filtered listings use the same per-set accounting. Missing legacy mean evidence stays unavailable.

What remains: current production validation still reads candidate-tape histories. It does not yet evaluate each subsequent gate from a newly simulated, independently owned predecessor-stage set. This reporting release does not claim that architectural work is complete.

Strategy switches and adjustments

The baseline run performed 114 walk-forward controls on the same tapes, one setting changed per case. These are diagnostic controls on the same historical window, not unseen profitability evidence. Cases requiring new tapes remain uncomputed. The repeat disables these already-recorded controls to reduce time and memory.
